item.title: From January 1, no petrol without pollution certificate at fuel stations in Odisha
item.description: Bhubaneswar: From January 1, 2026, vehicle owners in Odisha will not be able to buy petrol or diesel if they do not carry a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate. The Transport Department has decided to strictly enforce the rule to curb vehicular pollution and ensure compliance with emission norms. item.description: Bhubaneswar: Online ticket booking has begun for historical Odia play 'Ahe Nilashaila', which will be staged at Rabindra Mandap in Bhubaneswar from January 15, 2026 to January 18, 2026. item.title: Odisha’s Missing Children Crisis: 7,272 Still Untraced
item.description: Bhubaneswar: Despite multiple anti-trafficking initiatives and dedicated police units in the State, the growing number of missing children has emerged as a serious human rights concern in Odisha. The State continues to witness a steady rise in cases of children listed as missing with an overwhelming majority being minor girls. item.title: 139 villages in Odisha’s Malkangiri still without electricity, thousands live in darkness
item.description: Malkangiri: Even after repeated promises of rural electrification by the government, darkness continues to rule large parts of Odisha's Malkangiri district. According to information, electricity has not yet reached 139 villages in the district, forcing nearly 5,000 families to live without power supply.
